title: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Shell growth and surface chemistry of oleate-capped CdSe/ZnS core/shell quantum dots
citation: Synthetic fixture for pipeline testing; not a real publication.
materials: zinc-blende CdSe quantum dots (2.8 nm) overcoated with a thin ZnS shell
adsorbates: oleate (deprotonated oleic acid) as X-type surface ligand
objective: Determine the shell thickness, interface and surface termination of CdSe/ZnS core/shell quantum dots and how oleate binds to the shell surface.
key_findings: XRD shows zinc-blende reflections; the CdSe core lattice constant is 6.08 A and the peaks shift towards ZnS after shelling.
TEM gives a core diameter of 2.8 nm and an overall diameter of 3.9 nm after shelling.
ICP gives Zn:Cd = 1.6, consistent with two ZnS monolayers.
XPS shows no CdZnSe alloy signature.
1H NMR shows broadened vinyl resonances of bound oleate at about 2.5 ligands per nm^2.
author_interpretations: ZnS grows epitaxially as about two monolayers on the CdSe core with a sharp interface, compressing the core lattice.
The particles are Zn-rich at the surface and charge-balanced by X-type oleate bound to surface Zn.
reconstruction_target: Oleate-capped CdSe/ZnS core/shell quantum dot (2.8 nm core, ~2 ML ZnS shell)
